tasks.short: Develop and maintain document management standards and usage procedures.

steps.what: Review document-system behavior and choose required standards or procedure changes
Write standards and usage instructions from the verified procedure changes

loop.input: Verified procedure changes, demonstrated action sequence, current standard and approved terminology
loop.output: Draft instructions with source references for changed actions
loop.check: Specialist follows the instructions in a test library and checks intended access, revision and retention behavior, correcting omissions
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; absent demonstrated steps or failed walkthrough causes manual authoring
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative instructions must explain varied workflows. Native templates supply structure but cannot rewrite explanatory text from the change brief.

steps.what: Approve the final standard after checking control intent and executable user steps
Publish the approved standard in the controlled procedures library
Explain changed practices to document owners and resolve usage questions

tasks.design: Use native controlled templates in {DOCS}, with a bounded explanatory draft only where the specialist supplies verified procedure actions. Walk through the instructions and approve the complete final standard before controlled publication; explaining changed practices remains human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure text needs repeated rewriting when document-system controls change.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can reuse verified action sequences and terminology while native controls handle publication.
tasks.still_hard: Instructions must preserve policy intent and work for actual user permissions.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a usable standard that still preserves record integrity.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft writing, unchanged authority to define document practices.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a bounded model can rewrite verified procedure actions into draft guidance; executable walkthroughs and human acceptance remain necessary.

assumptions: Boundary covers standards selection, writing, approval, publication and owner explanation. This specialist is the delegated procedure approver; legal policy changes require the separate change-confirmation process.

s1 produces the actual action sequence, required permission, intended outcome, exception route, affected procedure ID and rationale. Missing action evidence requires manual demonstration before drafting.

s2 remaining includes source preparation, draft correction and a test-library walkthrough. s3 separately checks the final version and control intent after all edits; changed text must return for approval.
First try native {DOCS} templates and linked configuration fields. The model is used only for residual narrative, not deciding the standard. All baseline shares are provisional.
research_questions: Can a user with normal permissions execute the final instructions and achieve the intended result?

already_counted.description: Prepare evidence, correct instructions and walk through the draft
Check the final standard's intent and steps

incremental.description: Sample guidance after model or system changes

approvals.approved_version: Final standard revision and controlled-library destination approved in s3; later edits invalidate approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:17.5 drafting hours saved less two upkeep. Low: correction and walkthrough consume all drafting benefit. Same-library publication, standard choice and approval retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assist with assessment, acquisition and deployment of document management systems.

steps.what: Gather document management requirements and migration constraints from record owners
Assess candidate document systems with demonstrations and representative migration trials
Prepare system cost and requirement comparison tables
Advise procurement and the project lead on acquisition trade-offs
Support deployment planning and validate migrated sample documents and permissions
Check and record the specialist's final deployment assessment

tasks.design: Configure a structured comparison workbook in {SPREADSHEET} with fixed cost formulas and requirement rows. The specialist enters verified trial results and proposal costs, while demonstrations, acquisition advice and migration validation remain human; the final assessment is checked before recording in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparisons repeat cost calculations and table formatting between candidate systems.
tasks.enabler_now: A native workbook template can recalculate explicit cost assumptions without interpreting supplier promises.
tasks.still_hard: Vendor claims may not survive migration, access or records-retention trials.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a successful demonstration from a sustainable document-management capability.
tasks.altitude: Less comparison-table construction, unchanged advisory role in purchasing and deployment.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed requirement tables and cost formulas can support system comparison; demonstrations and migration acceptance remain expert work.

assumptions: Boundary is specialist assistance across evaluation, acquisition advice and deployment validation. Procurement signs the contract and the project lead authorizes production deployment through existing processes; neither action is claimed as removed labour here.

Proposals supply currency, license quantity, unit price, implementation cost, support cost, term and exclusions. s3 manually captures and verifies those values and s2 findings by requirement ID; absent prices or evidence remain unknown, not estimated by a model.
The project lead produces selected system decision and deployment plan after acquisition. s5 uses that later-phase input only after selection; the comparison does not assume its result.
Try a native {SPREADSHEET} table and formulas first. s3 retains entry and evidence checks; only formatting and arithmetic shrink. Shares are unmeasured.
research_questions: Does the comparison preserve one-time versus recurring costs and unverified requirements?

incremental.description: Maintain comparison formulas and requirement headings

approvals.approved_version: Completed specialist assessment and evidence references checked immediately before committing the exact record

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 7% removes 8 table-construction hours less 1 upkeep. Low assumes the comparison template already exists or proposal formats need manual treatment. Demonstrations, advice and deployment validation keep full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Administer document access and revision controls while protecting master records.

steps.what: Validate the access or revision-control request against document ownership and policy
Prepare the exact permission or revision-control configuration diff
Approve the final document-control diff and affected principals
Apply the approved access-rights or revision-control change
Verify effective permissions, version protection and master-document integrity
Draft the control-change audit record from request and configuration evidence
Check and commit the final control-change audit record

tasks.design: Configure permission and revision-control profiles in {DOCS}, generating an explicit diff for the document owner's approval before application. Preserve effective-permission and master-record checks, and prefill a {HELPDESK} audit draft from the approved change while the specialist enters and checks the verification outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Individual permissions and revision settings are changed through repetitive screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native profiles and approval flows can apply a reviewed diff without a model deciding access.
tasks.still_hard: Inherited permissions, external sharing and conflicts between revision protection and user needs.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a standard profile exposes a sensitive record or breaks its integrity.

ambition.what: Review inherited-access exceptions after each approved document-library reorganization.

tasks.altitude: Less repetitive control application, unchanged approval ownership and specialist verification responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native document profiles can apply approved permission and revision settings, but effective access still needs verification.

assumptions: Boundary is access and revision-control administration, not editing document content. The owner's 10% review is outside the focal denominator; no saving or new transfer is claimed for it.

Requester supplies document or library ID, principal ID, requested right, revision-control setting and reason. s1 checks policy; s2 captures the exact scope and rollback and uses profiles for repeated settings. Missing ownership or policy blocks application.
s6 copies request ID, approval ID, before/after values and timestamp; the specialist manually enters verification outcome within its remaining time. s7 retains the final check and commit.

Try native {DOCS} profiles, approval and audit exports first. Existing automatic audit logging earns no new saving; s6 represents a separate human change record only if present today. Shares are provisional.
research_questions: Does the applied diff produce exactly the approved effective rights under inheritance?

incremental.description: Maintain approved profiles and test inheritance edge cases

approvals.approved_version: Exact permission/revision diff, principals, scope and rollback approved by document owner in s3; edits void approval
Completed control audit draft including actual verification outcome checked immediately before saving

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Focal baseline 90, removed work 10 profile-preparation +25 application +4.9 audit drafting =39.9, giving central net 42.33% after 2 upkeep. Low assumes profile preparation and application mostly remain manual, with limited audit-copying return. Owner review and effective-access checks retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare official document changes and confirm them with legal and records management staff.

steps.what: Establish the requested official-document changes and required legal reviewers
Prepare revised official text and the rationale for each change
Prepare the version comparison and change-record draft for review
Confirm the final document and recorded changes with legal and records-management reviewers
Verify all required confirmations bind the final official revision and change record
Commit the confirmed official revision as the controlled master document
Commit the confirmed change record to the official revision history

tasks.design: Use native tracked changes, comparison and version-bound review in {DOCS}. Assemble the change-record draft from the actual diff and manually written rationales, obtain required legal and records-management confirmation of the final package, then commit master and history as separate gated actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Version comparison, reviewer confirmation and history entry happen through disconnected copies.
tasks.enabler_now: Native comparison and approval flows can bind confirmations to a document hash and its change record.
tasks.still_hard: Determining legal meaning and ensuring every required reviewer accepted the same final revision.
tasks.human_edge: Identify substantive policy changes and unresolved objections that prevent release.
tasks.altitude: Less comparison copying and history entry, unchanged legal approval ownership.

reach.learn: Approval provenance and immutable revision histories

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native document comparison and version-bound approval can generate change records from actual diffs without interpreting legal meaning.

assumptions: Boundary includes preparation, legal/records confirmation, master update and change history. The reviewer role represents all reviewers required by the existing policy; its 15% labour is excluded from the focal denominator and unchanged.

The requester supplies document ID, proposed changes and reason. s2 writes final text and rationale; only repeated layout and tracked-change preparation shrink. s3 uses old/new revision hashes, changed passages and s2 rationale; missing rationale blocks confirmation.

s4 includes returning requested edits to s2, regenerating s3 and obtaining final confirmation after all changes. No confirmation survives an edit. s5 checks the complete required confirmation set before allowing release.

First test native {DOCS} comparison, tracked changes and approval configuration. Existing automatic revision history earns no saving; s7 is included only for a separate current manual history-entry action. All shares are provisional.
research_questions: Can the system reject release when one required confirmation refers to an older revision?

already_counted.description: Verify the final version and complete reviewer confirmation set

incremental.description: Maintain reviewer routing and change-record layout

approvals.approved_version: Final official document hash and required reviewer confirmations completed in s4, verified in s5; any edit invalidates release
Final change-record draft and document hash confirmed together in s4; any regenerated diff requires new confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: nine drafting and fifteen comparison shares saved from85 focal shares, less two upkeep points, below net26.24. Low: existing comparison tools leave only a small formatting gain. Master and history saves and reviewer work retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use native document controls to reduce repeated clerical actions while retaining policy, legal and access decisions.
reach: Information security engineer access and integrity review
role.ambitious_version: Keep official records and procedures current with traceable approvals and less duplicate administration.
